who_what.text: The official README describes Forgetful as an open-source MCP storage and retrieval tool for agents, with HTTP and CLI interfaces to a shared knowledge base. No individual maintainer identity is asserted.

architecture.text: The application separates routes, service logic, repository protocols, and SQLite/PostgreSQL adapters. Bootstrap composes the database, embedding/reranking providers, services, optional activity events, and MCP registry.

Memory records hold atomic title/content/context concepts with keywords, tags, importance, project associations, and optional links to documents, code artifacts, files, and skills. SQLite stores vectors through sqlite-vec; PostgreSQL uses pgvector.

Retrieval is dense by default. Optional hybrid mode adds FTS5 or PostgreSQL full-text ranking and combines rankings with reciprocal-rank fusion; optional cross-encoder reranking and one-hop link expansion add later stages.

behavior.text: **Write.** Clients explicitly submit atomic memories with descriptive fields and optional project/resource links. The service applies configured provenance defaults, persists the memory, then can search and create similarity links in separate repository operations.

**Update and delete.** Partial field updates are supported. The documented obsolete lifecycle is a soft state with a reason and optional replacement; obsolete entries remain directly readable but are excluded from active retrieval. Physical erasure from backups or all stored copies is not established by this review.

**Retrieval.** User-scoped vector search returns primary records; optional reranking, one-hop links, project filtering, importance filtering, and token/count budgets shape the result. Hybrid keyword/vector fusion is opt-in. Project filters also constrain linked memories only when strict filtering is enabled.

**Scope isolation.** Repository methods receive authenticated user IDs and apply ownership filters. Project IDs further narrow organization/search, but no adversarial access test was run and no deployment authorization guarantee is claimed here.

**Provenance.** Optional source and encoding metadata can be stored and operator defaults can be applied. These values are assertions carried with records, not proof of truth or an adjudicated source trail.

metrics.evidence: Dense and optional hybrid retrieval are visible in code and docs; no answerability or abstention workload was evaluated.
Patch updates and an obsolete lifecycle are documented; no correction or staleness probes were run.
Obsolete records leave active search, while physical erasure across backups/copies was not established; no leakage probes were run.
User-ID filters and optional project filters are visible in repositories; no adversarial cross-user workload was run.
Provenance fields record asserted source metadata; no returned claim was adjudicated against evidence.
Search and indexing paths are source-visible; no timings were collected.
Result budgets, provider choices, relational storage and vector indexes are visible; no token, cost or bytes-per-memory measurement was made.
Logging, optional activity events and access counters are source-visible; no live reliability or telemetry interval was collected.

limits.text: This review inspected current source and documentation at the verified SHA; it did not run Forgetful, tests, or benchmarks, and establishes no retrieval quality, correction quality, calibrated abstention, deletion leakage, adversarial isolation, backend parity, provider behavior, or production reliability.

The security policy warns that HTTP listens on all network interfaces and runs without authentication unless configured. Deployment exposure therefore depends on operator binding, authentication, and TLS setup; this review did not exercise a deployment.
The search guide reports synthetic retrieval comparisons on an upstream corpus. Those figures are upstream-reported, were not reproduced here, and are not Forgetful benchmark results.

benchmark.note: No Forgetful runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was executed for this review.
